I know it sounds crazy, but the way she glances at her phone, or how she sometimes stays a bit later after her shift at the clinic… it all just adds up in my head. I’ve tried to look for concrete proof, you know, checking her mileage, looking through her texts when she’s not around, but I haven't found anything conclusive. Still, I just *know* it in my gut.

This whole thing started up about nine months ago, right after her new colleague joined. Honestly, it’s really put a strain on things at home. We used to be so close, but now I’m constantly on edge, constantly questioning her. It makes me feel pretty low, too. I've had some down days where I just don't feel like myself, a real sadness that's stuck around for a few weeks here and there, making it hard to focus even at work. But even when those low moods lift, or aren't so bad, that feeling about Sarah... that never goes away. I'm usually a good supervisor, keep the line running smoothly, and I'm still doing my job okay, but this constant worry about my wife is truly debilitating."
